chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a mukatabah (manumission contract) between two partners, where one of them frees his share: How should the servant act? He said: 'She serves the other [partner] one day and serves herself one day.' I said: 'If she dies and leaves wealth?' He said: 'The wealth is split in half between the one who freed [his share] and the one who retained [his share].'

key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: Manumission contract where a slave pays a fixed sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: How is the service and estate of a jointly-owned mukatab slave distributed when one owner frees his share?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the operational mechanics of a *mukatab* (slave seeking freedom through installments) who is jointly owned, establishing a rotational service model where she serves the remaining partner one day and her own emancipation the next. The ruling on inheritance upon death underscores the principle of proportional ownership, ensuring that any accumulated wealth is split equally between the manumitting partner and the one retaining his share, reflecting the practical application of partnership laws in early Shia jurisprudence.
